title: Warm Malty Cheddar Dip
description: A mild lager reduction and a butter roux carry sharp cheddar in a smooth, warm dip for soft potatoes or chicken.

steps.title: Reduce the lager
steps.text: Simmer {beer} in the HexClad for 4–6 minutes until reduced to about half its starting volume. Pour into the heatproof cup.

steps.title: Cook the mustard roux
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the emptied pan. Whisk in {flour} and {mustard} over low heat for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken the milk base
steps.text: Whisk {milk} and the reduced lager into the roux in stages. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Melt the cheddar
steps.text: Remove the skillet from the heat and whisk in {cheese} gradually until smooth.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Measure about 1 1/2 cups, loosening with warm water as needed. Spoon warm over potatoes or serve in small dipping bowls beside sauced chicken.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Reduce the lager a day ahead. Grate the cheddar shortly before making the dip. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Cheddar can separate when the finished dip freezes. For freezer prep, freeze the thickened milk base for up to 1 month and add the cheese after reheating. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses lager and mustard. For gentler Option B, replace the lager with low-sodium chicken broth and omit the mustard. For dairy-free dip, use avocado oil, unsweetened oat milk and a mild melting dairy-free cheddar. Calories include all of the measured beer before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 87 kcal, 4.4 g protein, 4.0 g total carbohydrate, 5.4 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 95 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
